en: Turning back to the text, one further maintains superior goodness to successively adorn it. May the Holy Sovereign of the present Great Tang see his sacred life flourish ever more;
may the golden wheel and the sun-wheel turn together, and may the days of Emperor Shun [shine forth].
The Buddha-sun rises high, surveying the hundred kings; ever new throughout ten thousand kalpas. The Imperial Heir is like the hidden stars;
the young sea is clear and serene;
the bedrock of the realm is raised ever higher.
Since this city serves as a bulwark,
we have maintained superior merit and virtue to adorn it in succession;
now, we pray that the six venerable masters may long enjoy the imperial bounty.
He served as the State Preceptor for Consecration,
permanently presiding over the Imperial Terrace and assisting the Enlightened Sovereign in his governance and transformation of the realm.
Next, we uphold the supreme goodness and employ it as adornment for the Grand Master, the General Superintendent of the Sangha.
We humbly pray that his mountain of wisdom may rise loftily and his ocean of virtue may be vast and deep.
May your life be as enduring as pine and cypress,
and your blessings and prosperity far-reaching;
may you thus long enjoy the imperial favor.
He perpetually fanned the breeze of compassion;
his illustrious reputation overflowed throughout the world,
and his elegant conduct flowed through this age of semblance.
Next, holding the supreme goodness, it is used in turn for adornment; may your noble personage,
Minister, find that the mountain of merit remains forever firm and your divine lifespan be boundless.
His meritorious achievements tower above the clouds and mountains;
his virtue and magnanimity are deeper than the vast ocean.
He went forth bearing the insignia of command to bring peace to the myriad regions.
Entering the Hall of Audience, you serve as a model for the hundred officials;
encountering the first day of the New Year, may you ever preserve the springtime.
May your destiny be like the pine and cypress, and your longevity equal that of the kalpa-stone.
Furthermore, may you employ these supreme merits next to adorn yourself. We, your great subjects, pray that your form shall be like the great earth, enduring for a thousand years;
and that your constant peace and blessings shall rival the mountains and rivers, remaining forever firm throughout ten thousand ages.
Thereafter, he spread his fragrant reputation throughout the imperial capital;
with wings outstretched upon the celestial thoroughfare,
he circulated his elegant fame at the Court of the Phoenix (Luan-chi) and washed his scales in the waters of the Han.
Furthermore, these superior and virtuous [inscriptions] are used in succession as adornments to enshrine the two Attendants Yao and An.
We humbly pray that their jade towers shall soar beyond the heavens and their purple canopies shall fly upon the celestial pathways.
May your life be as long as Heaven and your blessings as vast as Earth.
May you be preserved from all calamities, finding peace in every movement and stillness.
As you face the eight directions, may your coming and going be pure and auspicious.

Next, uphold supreme goodness and employ it as adornment; may the descendants of the state ministers inherit the favor of a thousand autumns and eternally dwell in the glory of ten thousand generations,
perfecting both loyalty and filial piety.
The succession of the noble house continues:
next is Chishi Shōzen, followed by Yūjō Sōgon, and others who serve as instructors in the Buddhist tradition.
We humbly pray that their honor and prosperity may ever renew, and that their fragrant reputations may spread like clouds across the heavens.
Entering the throne of faith and emerging as the leader of the monastic community,
you cause all sentient beings to ascend to higher realms according to their kind;
you constantly provide the precious raft upon the ocean of suffering.
Next, uphold the supreme virtues and employ them as adornments for the laws and regulations of the Śākya school.
May your physical strength and vitality increase and be firmly established,
and may your lifespan extend as long as a lingering cloud.
May you always serve as a bridge across the ocean of suffering and act as a bulwark for the Dharma-gate.
May your successive merits and blessings successively adorn you, O Prefectural Governor and others.
May your life span be long and far-reaching; as days pass and months come,
may blessings and auspiciousness shine upon one another,
enduring as long as heaven and earth.
Next, may you uphold supreme merit and employ it for adornment; may the various officials and attendants alike wish for your prosperity and long life, and may they serve you with joy and diligence.
May your fame and reputation flourish daily, and may your lineage prosper and thrive.
His glorious reputation was as vast as the clouds, and his city-walls and altars were ablaze with splendor;
he exhausted himself in loyalty,
and the officials of his tribes likewise burned with devotion.
May they be solely pure and upright.
Next, may they uphold supreme merit and employ it to adorn the venerable elders and great virtuous ones,
who long extend their exemplary instructions to rectify and protect the citadel of the Dharma.
May the lamp of compassion shine forever to uphold the discipline of the Buddhist realm.
May the Great Virtuous Dharma Generals and others, who successively maintain supreme goodness and successively employ it as adornment,
cause the mountain of wisdom to stand lofty and the water of virtue to be clear and pure.
The branches of dhyāna flourish and the flowers of awakening bloom;
the fragrance of the precepts perfumes and the pearl of wisdom shines brightly.
Next, may this superior merit be employed to adorn all the virtuous bhikṣuṇīs.
I only pray that the four reliances may be ever fulfilled and the six perfections practiced with single-minded diligence;
that the tree of the mind may be eternally in bloom and the lamp of the heart forever radiant;
and that the water of eight virtues may wash away defilements and dispel calamities.
Adorned with seven kinds of pure and wondrous flowers,
the Dharma-body is further embellished by holding supreme merit, as well as official seals, staffs, and other regalia.
We pray that your longevity may equal that of the pine and cypress, and your blessings may rival those of the rivers and lakes.
May you live ten thousand years and a thousand autumns, neither by wind nor by change.
Next, take up this supreme merit and employ it for adornment—[as an offering] to the staffs of our elders and others.
May we, upon hearing this but once, attain awakening in a thousand ways and realize the Great Dhāraṇī.
May the stains of transgression be eliminated in no time,
and may the sprouts of merit and virtue flourish. Furthermore,
may you receive auspicious blessings throughout the spring and autumn, and may the cold and heat be favorable and harmonious.
May they preserve wealth and honor for a thousand ages and manifest auspiciousness throughout successive kalpas. Furthermore,
may the eminent merit be maintained and used for adornment by Master Li and the others.
However, this humble servant has long been graced by your instructions and has received your teachings within the Hall of Excellence;
I only regret that during my lifetime I could not fully follow your guidance.
After my passing, I shall feel ashamed to ascend the Dharma seat;
reflecting thus, I redouble my efforts to offer these objects of praise and dedication.
First, I pray that your spirit may roam the Nala Garden, reverently seeking the truth through the awakening of the Buddha.
In the evening, one respectfully adorns the flower pedestal with the fragrance of the precepts to serve the Holy Golden Wheel, which revolves and turns incessantly.
One constantly hastens through the garden of joy, where the chambers flourish for such excursions;
far-reaching, one floats upon the waters of merit.
Next, by means of supreme merit and further adornment, may such-and-such [person] traverse the path of the soul born of their parents.
We humbly pray that they may tread with feet upon golden soil and roam their spirits within the realm of the immortals.
Crossing the boat of compassion upon the waters of meditative concentration, he forever dried up the river of delusion;
brandishing the sword of wisdom amidst the timber of conditioned phenomena, he long protected those who receive [his grace].
Among his own kin, he achieved purity and integrity, while those far removed from him—both branches and twigs alike—were universally moistened and benefited.
